title: Fibre cotangent comparison after localization with generator bound
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak q\subset A$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $F=k\otimes_R A$, $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ with $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\bar\lambda\bar a$, and $L=\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Module localization has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and finite-dimensional vector-space dimension that of [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Let $M=\Omega_{A/R}$ and $N=\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The homomorphism $A\to L$ induces $A_{\mathfrak q}\to L$, and the differential base-change isomorphism $\beta:N\xrightarrow{\sim}F\otimes_A M$ induces a canonical $L$-linear isomorphism $\theta:M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}L\xrightarrow{\sim}N\otimes_F L$. Its value on $(\omega/a)\otimes\lambda$, for $a\notin\mathfrak q$, is $\beta^{-1}(1\otimes\omega)\otimes(\lambda/\bar a)$; its inverse sends $\beta^{-1}(b\otimes\omega)\otimes\lambda$ to $(\omega/1)\otimes\bar b\lambda$, where $\bar b$ is the image of $b\in F$ in $L$. If $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ generate $M_{\mathfrak q}$ over $A_{\mathfrak q}$, with $r\geq0$, then $\theta(m_i\otimes1)$ span $N\otimes_F L$ over $L$ and $\dim_L(N\otimes_F L)\leq r$.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), followed by localization and tensor comparison for the displayed equality in Morphisms Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), clause (4).

proof.text: First check the denominators. The residue map $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ has kernel $\mathfrak q$: indeed $a/1\in\mathfrak q A_{\mathfrak q}$ implies $ta\in\mathfrak q$ for some $t\notin\mathfrak q$, hence $a\in\mathfrak q$ by primality; the converse is immediate. Thus $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps to nonzero elements of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The ring localization universal property extends $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ to $R_{\mathfrak p}$; it kills $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and therefore factors through $k$. The tensor relations give the stated map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Its kernel $\mathfrak Q$ is prime, since the target is a field, and its inverse image in $A$ is $\mathfrak q$. Consequently $a\notin\mathfrak q$ has image outside $\mathfrak Q$, so its image $\bar a$ in $L=\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$ is nonzero. Apply the same localization universal property to $A\to L$, obtaining $A_{\mathfrak q}\to L$, $c/t\mapsto\bar c/\bar t$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), and Section 07BH (residue fields); tensor universal property, Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: Apply differential base change with $R'=k$ and $S=A$. The $F$-module form of [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] gives the canonical isomorphism $F\otimes_A M\xrightarrow{\sim}N$. Its inverse is exactly the map $\beta$ in the statement; in particular $\beta^{-1}$ is $F$-linear. No finiteness or flatness of $A/R$ is required here.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), with the equivalent scalar-extension form of its canonical isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the standard localization-tensor equivalence $M_{\mathfrak q}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_A M$, sending $\omega/a$ to $(1/a)\otimes\omega$, and extend scalars to $L$. After commuting the outer tensor factors, cancellation [lem-trf-scalar-tensor-cancel-base-change] identifies $L\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}(A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_A M)$ with $L\otimes_A M$. The map on $z\otimes(\omega/a)$ is $(z/\bar a)\otimes\omega$: the extension $\rho$ sends $1/a$ to $\bar a^{-1}$, as follows by multiplying by the nonzero $\bar a$. The inverse sends $z\otimes\omega$ to $z\otimes(\omega/1)$. In Lean these are LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct and AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, including their pure-tensor formulas.

source.place: Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module), fraction relation preceding it; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product). This writes out the localization cancellation used after Tag 00RV.

proof.text: Apply cancellation [lem-trf-scalar-tensor-cancel-base-change] again to $A\to F\to L$, obtaining $L\otimes_F(F\otimes_A M)\cong L\otimes_A M$, with $z\otimes(b\otimes\omega)\mapsto(\bar b z)\otimes\omega$ and inverse $z\otimes\omega\mapsto z\otimes(1\otimes\omega)$. Compose the first cancellation with the inverse of this one, scalar extension of $\beta^{-1}$, and outer tensor symmetries. Tensor symmetry is made $L$-linear using exactly the transported right-factor actions in ComparisonAlong. This composite is $\theta$. The pure-tensor formulas for the localization equivalence, cancellation, and scalar extension give both asserted formulas, including the inverse formula.

source.place: Tags 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), explicit balanced cancellation after Tag 00RV.

proof.text: If the $m_i$ generate $M_{\mathfrak q}$, write any $m\in M_{\mathfrak q}$ as $m=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i m_i$ with $c_i\in A_{\mathfrak q}$. Then $m\otimes\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\otimes\bar c_i\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^r(\bar c_i\lambda)(m_i\otimes1)$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so the $m_i\otimes1$ span the source of $\theta$. Applying the surjective $L$-linear map $\theta$ shows that the $r$ displayed images span $N\otimes_F L$. This also applies to the empty family: its span is zero.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), pure-tensor generation and balancing; the generator implication used in Morphisms Tag 01V9, clause (4).

proof.text: The image family has $r$ elements and spans by step 5. Its range is finite, so its span is a finitely generated $L$-module; since that span is the whole target, the target is finite dimensional. The elementary dimension inequality for a finite spanning family gives $\dim_L(N\otimes_F L)\leq r$, directly implemented by Mathlib finrank_le_of_span_eq_top. This avoids separately extracting an independent subfamily. It includes $r=0$, when the span is zero and the whole target has dimension zero.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), clause (4), elementary linear-algebra completion via the two cited Mathlib leaves.
